text:
Sophie (support): hi folks — getting a handful of escalations this morning about p95/p99 spikes on the text-generation API since ~03:00 UTC. customers reporting timeouts and UI jank. sample from ACME ticket: p95 ~820ms (baseline ~140ms), p99 ~2.1s. stack=hosted, model=redwood-ggml-3b, route=/v1/generate

Kevin (eng-runtime): ugh. any commonalities? region, model variant, or route params?

Sophie (support): all in us-west, same model and route. a few mentions of longer prompts but nothing extreme. Slack traces attached in ticket show high backend latency, and internal logs show a bunch of "kv_cache MISS" lines around the time.

Kevin (eng-runtime): kv_cache MISS — interesting. we've had a higher eviction churn in the last deploy? deploy-bot: deployed runtime v2.14.3 at 02:45 UTC to us-west (canary->prod).

deploy-bot: rollback available: v2.14.2. use `/deploy rollback us-west v2.14.2`

AJ (sre): I'm pulling metrics now. PromQL I ran: `sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) by (instance)` and `sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) by (instance)`. miss rate jumped from ~5% -> ~38% around 02:55.

AJ (sre): full query I used: `100 * (sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m])) / (sum(rate(kv_cache_hits_total[5m])) + sum(rate(kv_cache_misses_total[5m]))))`

Maria (prod): that aligns with alert we muted for late-night testing. Is it possible the new eviction policy made LFU->LRU change? I remember a config change in the release notes.

Kevin (eng-runtime): yes the PR swapped eviction from fixed-LRU to an adaptive LFU/LRU hybrid to try to improve long-tail prefix retention. but it included a bug where keys with ephemeral suffixes weren't normalized, increasing cardinality for prefix cache.

Sophie (support): TL;DR: higher miss rate -> more work on runtime -> extra latency. customers hitting tails. What's the immediate mitigation?

Kevin (eng-runtime): short term: rollback the eviction algorithm (deploy v2.14.2) to stop thrash. medium term: fix the key normalization to avoid per-request unique keys for prefix cache.

AJ (sre): I can trigger a canary rollback to verify improvement. plan: canary us-west-1a (10%) -> monitor kv_cache_miss rate and p95 for 15m -> if stable, full rollback.

Leo (devex): can we also prewarm hot prefixes to reduce cold miss impact while rollback is in progress? I can run a short seeder job hitting top N prefixes.

Kevin (eng-runtime): yes. also add a temporary rule to bypass prefix caching for endpoints that include any `session_id` param — that'll reduce spurious keys until we fix normalization.

Sophie (support): will communicate to affected customers we have a mitigation and expected rollback. any repro steps for the engineering team?

Kevin (eng-runtime): repro steps I used locally to reproduce thrash:
```bash
# simulate 200 concurrent clients cycling through many prefixes
for i in {1..200}; do
  PREFIX=\"user_prompt_$((RANDOM%10000))\"
  curl -s -X POST https://internal-loadgen.us-west/internal/generate \\\
    -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TEST_TOKEN\" \\\
    -d \"{\\\"model\\\":\\\"redwood-ggml-3b\\\",\\\"prompt\\\":\\\"$PREFIX: do something\\\"}\" &
done
wait
```
This drives the prefix key cardinality up and causes eviction thrash. Locally I watched `kv_cache_live_keys` spike.

AJ (sre): also look at this debug endpoint for cache state: `GET /admin/cache/stats` — sample output:
```
{
  "total_keys": 124312,
  "evictions_1m": 1932,
  "hit_rate_5m": 61.2,
  "miss_rate_5m": 38.8
}
```
When miss_rate_5m > 30% we see p95 regressions.

Maria (prod): notes for rollout: if we rollback, watch `p95_generation` and `kv_cache_miss_rate` and customer tickets. set a temporary alert: `kv_cache_miss_rate > 25` for 5m.

Kevin (eng-runtime): root cause summary: the new adaptive eviction combined with a cache-key bug (ephemeral suffix included) increased effective cache cardinality and eviction churn -> higher miss rates -> backend did extra compute and blocked GPU slots -> p95/p99 regressions.

Kevin (eng-runtime): code snippet of bug (pseudo):
```python
# before: normalized prefix
key = f\"prefix:{normalize(prompt_prefix)}\"
# bug introduced: ephemeral id concatenated
key = f\"prefix:{normalize(prompt_prefix)}:{request.id}\"
```
That `request.id` made nearly every request unique.

Sophie (support): Thanks — can you give me the short message to send to customers?

Maria (prod): Suggested customer-facing blurb:
"We're investigating increased latency for text generation in us-west. We identified an internal caching regression causing higher cache-miss rates and are rolling back a recent runtime change. We'll monitor and update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption."

Sophie (support): perfect, sending now. :thumbsup:

AJ (sre): I'll start canary rollback now. kicking it off.

deploy-bot: started rollback to v2.14.2 in us-west (canary 10%) at 03:12 UTC

AJ (sre): canary results after 10m: kv_cache_miss_rate -> 6%, p95 back to ~160ms. Looks good. starting full rollback.

deploy-bot: rollback to v2.14.2 complete in us-west at 03:28 UTC

Kevin (eng-runtime): after rollback, evictions down, hit_rate back up. I'll open PR to fix key normalization + add unit test and a lint rule to prevent concatenating request ids into cache keys.

Kevin (eng-runtime): medium-term actions:
- normalize cache keys for prefixes (PR opened)
- add cardinality guard: if prefix cardinality > X, disable caching for that route
- add backpressure/circuit-breaker to avoid blocking GPUs on cache misses
- prewarm hot prefixes on startup

Maria (prod): assign owners: Kevin -> fix + PR, AJ -> add alert & run canary rollback runbook, Leo -> prewarm job, Sophie -> customer comms. target: hotfix in next 4 hours.

Kevin (eng-runtime): will push PR and request expedited review. linking to draft: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/5632

Sophie (support): closing loop with customers; will update tickets with root cause and mitigation.

Leo (devex): I'll add a dashboard tile showing `kv_cache_miss_rate` vs `p95_generation` so support can correlate quickly.

AJ (sre): logging final: observed p95 drop from 820ms -> 150ms after rollback. marking this resolved for now, but leaving follow-up action items.

Sophie (support): thanks team. I'll keep the thread open until PR lands and we verify no recurrence.

Kevin (eng-runtime): thanks all. short-term postmortem notes: cache-key bug + eviction policy change = cache thrash -> regression. follow-up in #postmortems once PR merges.
